title: Chanting Sutras, Holding Mantras, and Reciting the Buddha's Name
author: Annotated by Zhanran
excerpt: Directly clarify the ground of the mind, dissolve everything back into self-nature, and practice as taught.

inline.s: Directly clarify the ground of the mind, dissolve everything back into self-nature, and practice as taught.
asked about the method of holding sutras and mantras. The Bodhisattva said: 'What is called holding sutras and mantras is holding one's own mind. The key is to

directly clarify the ground of the mind. If one only says one has recited them until familiar and chanted them many times, and has recited such-and-such a sutra, such-and-such a mantra, or such-and-such a Buddha, claiming to have great merit, yet cannot dissolve every line back into self-nature, nor deeply understand the Tathāgata's wondrous truth

, and claims that one can thereby attain realization — has one not seen those at the crossroads, the eyeless, the footless, the beggar-women and beggar-men, who recite without pause from morning till night, so that what they recite in a year amounts to no less than
several hundred thousand times? Yet they remain

the disabled and the beggars, and have not realized so much as a hair's breadth of attainment. Why is this? Simply because they have neither understanding nor practice. Therefore we know that to hold this sutra, one should practice according to this sutra

. And one should make great vows, whether to seek birth in a Buddha-land, to seek to clarify the ground of the mind, to develop great wisdom, or to benefit and rescue living beings. All these rely on the Tathāgata's vast and far-reaching power to bring the practitioner's vows to fulfillment. Only in this way is it truly holding sutras, holding mantras, and reciting the Buddha's name.']

Someone asked about the method of holding sutras and mantras. The Bodhisattva Jueming Miaoxing said: 'What is called holding sutras and mantras is holding one's own mind and making it correspond with the sutras and mantras, and the key is to directly clarify the ground of the mind. If one only says one has recited them until familiar and chanted them many times, and has recited such-and-such a sutra, such-and-such a mantra, or such-and-such a Buddha, and thereby thinks one has great merit, yet cannot dissolve every line back into self-nature, nor deeply understand the Tathāgata's subtle and wondrous truth, and then says one can thereby gain merit — such a person has not seen those at the crossroads, the disabled ones without eyes or feet, and the beggars, men and women, who recite without pause from early morning till night, so that in a year they recite no less than several hundred thousand times. Yet they remain the disabled and the beggars, and have not realized the slightest bit of merit. Why is this? Simply because they have neither understanding nor practice. Therefore we know that to hold this sutra, one should practice according to this sutra. And one should also make great vows, whether to seek birth in a Buddha-land, to seek to clarify the ground of the mind, to develop great wisdom, or to benefit and rescue living beings. And all these vows rely on the Tathāgata's vast and far-reaching power to empower the practitioner so that they may be fulfilled. Only in this way is it truly holding sutras, holding mantras, and reciting the Buddha's name.'
Here, the Bodhisattva Jueming Miaoxing instructs on the method of chanting sutras, holding mantras, and reciting the Buddha's name:
Directly clarify the ground of the mind, dissolve everything back into self-nature, and practice as taught.

[What is called holding sutras and mantras is holding one's own mind] What is called holding sutras and mantras is holding one's own mind and making it correspond with the sutras and mantras. Therefore the Bodhisattva Jueming Miaoxing then instructed:
directly clarify the ground of the mind”
“therefore we know that to hold this sutra, one should practice according to this sutra

. [Ground of the mind] The mind is the root of all dharmas and can give rise to all dharmas, hence the mind is called the 'ground of the mind.' Also, because practitioners act in accordance with the mind, the mind is called the 'ground of the mind.' [Directly clarify the ground of the mind] To directly remove the deluded thoughts, greed, anger, and ignorance in the mind, restoring the mind to clarity and purity. [Dissolve every line back into self-nature] To apply every line to one's own mental conduct, turning self-nature from delusion to awakening. The Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch says:
When self-nature is deluded, one is an ordinary being; when self-nature is awakened, one is a Buddha.”
